[PROPOSED] INTERIM ORDER ON PLAINTIFF’S REQUEST FOR INTERIM
RELIEF PENDING DETERMINATION OF HIS RULE 72(a) OBJECTIONS TO ECF
NO. 84

This matter is before the Court on the request for interim relief contained in Plaintiff’s Rule
72(a) Objections to ECF No. 84 and Motion to Set Aside the Amendment and Discovery Denials
and for Coordinated Determination of the Pending Objections (ECF No. __). Having considered
the request, the pending objections at ECF Nos. 66 and 67 with their supporting memorandum at
ECF No. 68, the motion at ECF No. 76, and the record, and for the reasons stated in Plaintiff’s
Memorandum in Support, it is hereby

ORDERED that enforcement of the comparison requirement in the Order entered
September 9, 2026 (ECF No. 64) is SUSPENDED pending the Court’s determination of ECF Nos.
66, 67, and 76 and of Plaintiff’s objections to ECF No. 84 (ECF No. ___). This suspension does not

vacate ECF No. 84 and does not itself grant ECF No. 59; it is further

ORDERED that, while the suspension in the preceding paragraph operates, Plaintiff’s
Motion for Leave to File Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint (ECF No. 59) and the
proposed pleading at ECF No. 59-1 shall not be denied, stricken, deemed abandoned, excluded, or
otherwise adversely treated on the ground of nonproduction of the comparison directed by ECF
No. 64; it is further

ORDERED that the amendment-related issues presented in ECF Nos. 66, 67, and 76 and in
Plaintiff’s objections to ECF No. 84 shall be determined before, or expressly within, any
disposition of the pending motions to dismiss (ECF Nos. 10, 21, and 45) that would terminate a
claim and that depends on the identity of the operative pleading. Those motions remain pending,
and all briefing on them remains of record; it is further

ORDERED that the discovery objections presented in Plaintiff’s objections to ECF No. 84
shall be determined before, or expressly within, any adjudication that relies on the factual premises
addressed by the interrogatories at ECF Nos. 15-1 and 54-1. This paragraph does not reach issues
that do not depend on those premises; it is further

ORDERED that ECF Nos. 59, 59-1, 59-2, 60, 61, 74, 78, 78-1, and 83, and ECF Nos. 15,
15-1, 16, 31, 33, 36, 46, 52, 54, 54-1, 55, 73, and 81, remain of record as authorized submissions on
the matters to which they are directed; it is further

ORDERED that the Court may determine the matters identified in this Order together in a
single order; it is further

ORDERED that the fifth objection presented in Plaintiff’s objections to ECF No. 84, which
rests on the financial disclosure reports submitted as Exhibits A and B to Plaintiff’s Motion to
Disqualify Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis, and Plaintiff’s Motion for Targeted Vacatur of ECF

Nos. 64 and 84, Withdrawal or Modification of the Magistrate-Judge Referral, and Related Interim

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document90-2 Filed 10/13/26 Page 3 of 3 PagelD#

Relief (ECF No. ___) are preserved for coordinated determination. Nothing in this Order treats
ownership of the reported interest during the Magistrate Judge’s participation, or disqualification
under 28 U.S.C. § 455, as established, and nothing in this Order determines the disqualification
motion pending before the Magistrate Judge; it is further

ORDERED that all other proceedings in this action are unaffected by this Order; it is
further

ORDERED that the suspension in the first decretal paragraph expires upon entry of an
order determining the comparison requirement in ECF No. 64 and specifying its operative effect;
that the protection in the second decretal paragraph continues until ECF No. 59 is determined; and
that the sequencing directions in the third and fourth decretal paragraphs expire upon entry of the
order determining Plaintiff’s objections to ECF No. 84.

The Clerk is DIRECTED to send a copy of this Order to Plaintiff at his address of record
and to all counsel of record.

It is so ORDERED.

Alexandria, Virginia
, 2026

Rossie D. Alston, Jr.
United States District Judge
